images.title: A glass of lassi in twelfths
images.purpose: Show that fourths and thirds become the same unit, twelfths, so 1/4 + 1/3 = 3/12 + 4/12 = 7/12.
images.composition: One tall straight-sided steel glass in the centre with wide margins, labels to its right, and one sum line below.
images.exact_structure: One tall straight-sided glass drawn as a plain upright rectangle with a grey #6B7280 outline, marked inside by thin grey lines into 12 equal levels. From the bottom: 3 levels filled teal #0072B2 for curd, the next 4 levels filled amber #E69F00 for water, the top 5 levels plain. A thin reddish purple #CC79A7 brace on the right of the 7 filled levels. Centred below: one sum line. Exactly 1 glass, 12 equal levels, 3 teal, 4 amber, 5 plain.

images.takeaway: Make the units the same, then add the tops and keep the unit.
images.description: A glass marked in 12 equal levels: 3 teal levels of curd are 1/4 = 3/12 and 4 amber levels of water are 1/3 = 4/12, together 7/12 of the glass.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why the glass is marked in twelfths, then count the filled levels.

image_decisions.why: One glass in twelfths shows both parts in a common unit and the sum at once.
